story: As a shopper, I want my Aurora Storefront account to lock after too many wrong password attempts, so that nobody can guess their way into my account.
criteria:
Scenario: Lock after repeated failures
  Given a shopper with an active account
  When they enter a wrong password 5 times within 10 minutes
  Then the account is locked

Scenario: Lock duration
  Given a locked account
  When 30 minutes have not yet passed
  Then sign-in is refused even with the correct password

Scenario: The shopper is told
  Given the account has just locked
  When the lock message appears
  Then it names the 30 minute duration

Scenario: Counter resets
  Given a shopper has failed fewer than 5 times
  When they sign in successfully
  Then the failed attempt counter returns to zero

Scenario: Support unlock
  Given a locked account
  When support staff unlock it from the admin console
  Then the shopper can sign in straight away

cases.title: Account locks on the fifth wrong password within 10 minutes
cases.pre_conditions: Shopper 'dana.reed@example.com' has an active Aurora Storefront account and 0 recorded failed attempts
steps: Open the Aurora Storefront sign-in page
Enter 'dana.reed@example.com' in the email field
Enter 'WrongPass1!' in the password field and submit
Repeat the wrong password submission four more times within 10 minutes
Observe the response after the fifth submission
cases.expected_result: After the fifth failure the account state changes to Locked, the sign-in form is replaced by the lockout message, and no session cookie is issued
cases.bdd_scenario:
Given a shopper with an active account
And the account has no recorded failed attempts
When the shopper submits a wrong password 5 times within 10 minutes
Then the account is locked
And no session is created

cases.title: Locked account refuses the correct password for 30 minutes
steps: Open the sign-in page
Enter 'dana.reed@example.com' and the correct password 'RightPass9!'
Submit the form
cases.expected_result: Sign-in is refused, the lockout message is shown with the remaining time, and the audit log records a blocked attempt on a locked account
cases.bdd_scenario:
Given a locked account
And 30 minutes have not yet passed
When the shopper submits the correct password
Then sign-in is refused

cases.title: Lockout message names the 30 minute duration
cases.pre_conditions: Account 'dana.reed@example.com' has just reached its fifth failed attempt
steps: Trigger the fifth failed sign-in attempt
Read the message shown above the sign-in form
cases.expected_result: The message reads 'Your account is locked for 30 minutes.' and the duration is stated in minutes, not in a relative phrase such as 'a while'
cases.test_data: expected_copy=Your account is locked for 30 minutes.
cases.bdd_scenario:
Given the account has just locked
When the lock message appears
Then it names the 30 minute duration

cases.title: Successful sign-in resets the failed attempt counter
cases.pre_conditions: Account 'dana.reed@example.com' has 3 recorded failed attempts and is not locked
steps: Sign in with the correct password 'RightPass9!'
Sign out
Enter a wrong password twice
Check the stored failed attempt count
cases.expected_result: The counter is 0 immediately after the successful sign-in and 2 after the two later failures, so the account does not lock
cases.bdd_scenario:
Given a shopper has failed fewer than 5 times
When they sign in successfully
Then the failed attempt counter returns to zero

cases.title: Lockout message does not reveal whether the email is registered
cases.pre_conditions: The email 'nobody@example.com' has no Aurora Storefront account
steps: Submit 'nobody@example.com' with a wrong password five times
Compare the message with the one shown for a registered email
cases.expected_result: Both paths show the same generic message and the same response timing, so an attacker cannot tell registered emails from unregistered ones
cases.bdd_scenario:
Given an email with no account
When five wrong passwords are submitted
Then the response is indistinguishable from a registered email

cases.title: Password reset is still refused while the account is locked
steps: Open the sign-in page
Follow the 'Forgot password' link
Submit 'dana.reed@example.com'
cases.expected_result: The reset flow does not silently unlock the account; after setting a new password the shopper still waits out the remaining lock time
cases.bdd_scenario:
Given a locked account
When the shopper completes a password reset
Then the lock is still in force

cases.title: Four failures followed by the correct password do not lock the account
steps: Submit a wrong password four times within 10 minutes
Submit the correct password 'RightPass9!'
cases.expected_result: Sign-in succeeds on the fifth submission, the account is never locked, and the counter is reset to 0
cases.bdd_scenario:
Given a shopper with 0 failed attempts
When they fail 4 times and then succeed
Then the account is not locked

cases.title: Five failures spread over more than 10 minutes do not lock the account
cases.pre_conditions: Account 'dana.reed@example.com' has 0 recorded failed attempts and the clock can be controlled
steps: Submit a wrong password four times over 9 minutes
Advance the clock to 11 minutes after the first attempt
Submit a wrong password once more
cases.expected_result: The first attempt has fallen outside the 10 minute window, so only 4 attempts count and the account stays unlocked
cases.bdd_scenario:
Given four failures inside the window
When a fifth failure happens after the window has moved on
Then the account is not locked

cases.title: Sign-in works again at exactly 30 minutes after the lock
steps: Wait until the clock reads 30 minutes after the lock
Submit the correct password 'RightPass9!'
cases.expected_result: Sign-in succeeds at 30:00, and a check at 29:59 is still refused
cases.bdd_scenario:
Given an account locked 30 minutes ago
When the shopper submits the correct password
Then sign-in succeeds

cases.title: Failures from two browsers count towards the same account lock
cases.pre_conditions: Account 'dana.reed@example.com' has 0 recorded failed attempts; two browsers are open
steps: Submit three wrong passwords in browser A
Submit two wrong passwords in browser B within the same 10 minutes
Attempt to sign in from either browser
cases.expected_result: The counter is held per account, not per browser, so the fifth failure locks the account for both browsers
cases.bdd_scenario:
Given failures from two browsers
When the combined count reaches 5 within 10 minutes
Then the account is locked everywhere

cases.title: Lock survives closing and reopening the browser
steps: Close the browser completely
Reopen it and clear cookies
Submit the correct password 'RightPass9!'
cases.expected_result: The lock is stored against the account on the server, so a fresh browser is still refused and the message still names the remaining time
cases.bdd_scenario:
Given a locked account
When the shopper returns in a fresh browser
Then sign-in is still refused

failure_modes.title: Lockout counter is not shared across servers
failure_modes.effect: An attacker keeps guessing passwords past the fifth attempt, so the lock never protects the account
failure_modes.cause: Each web server counts failed attempts in its own memory instead of one shared store
failure_modes.severity_reason: The account can be taken over even though the lock looks like it works
failure_modes.likelihood_reason: Aurora Storefront already runs more than one web server behind a load balancer
failure_modes.detectability_reason: A one-server test environment never shows it
failure_modes.test_idea: Send the five failed sign-ins through two different servers and check the account still locks

failure_modes.title: Lockout message tells an attacker that the email is registered
failure_modes.effect: An attacker harvests a list of registered shopper emails from the sign-in form
failure_modes.cause: The locked reply differs from the reply for an email nobody has registered
failure_modes.severity_reason: Leaked emails feed phishing, but no account is entered directly
failure_modes.likelihood_reason: The two replies are written by different parts of the code
failure_modes.detectability_reason: Reading the two replies side by side shows it at once
failure_modes.test_idea: Compare the reply for a locked registered email with the reply for an email nobody registered

failure_modes.title: Lockout email arrives long after the lock when the site is busy
failure_modes.effect: The shopper never learns the account was locked and calls support instead
failure_modes.cause: One worker drains the notification queue and falls behind at peak hours
failure_modes.severity_reason: Support cost and a frustrated shopper, no data loss
failure_modes.likelihood_reason: Peak traffic already queues other mail
failure_modes.detectability_reason: On a quiet test environment the mail always arrives instantly
failure_modes.test_idea: Lock 200 accounts in one minute and measure when the last notification is delivered

failure_modes.title: Clock drift between servers makes the 10 minute window wrong
failure_modes.effect: Attempts land in the wrong window, so some shoppers are stopped after three tries and others are never stopped
failure_modes.cause: Every server stamps an attempt with its own clock and the clocks drift apart
failure_modes.severity_reason: Shoppers are shut out of an account that is working
failure_modes.likelihood_reason: Time sync fails quietly on one host now and then
failure_modes.detectability_reason: Nothing in the product reports drift, so it looks like a random bug
failure_modes.test_idea: Move the clock on one server forward by two minutes and repeat the five attempt run

failure_modes.title: A screen reader does not announce the lockout message
failure_modes.effect: A shopper using a screen reader hears nothing and keeps retrying a locked account
failure_modes.cause: The message is swapped into the page without a live region, so assistive technology ignores it
failure_modes.severity_reason: The feature is unusable for part of the audience
failure_modes.likelihood_reason: Live regions are easy to leave out of a swapped-in message
failure_modes.detectability_reason: Only a run with a screen reader shows it
failure_modes.test_idea: Trigger the lock with a screen reader running and check the message is read out

failure_modes.title: The failed attempt counter is not cleared after a password reset
failure_modes.effect: A shopper who has just reset their password is shut out again after two mistakes
failure_modes.cause: The reset flow stores the new password but never touches the stored attempt counter
failure_modes.severity_reason: The shopper cannot buy anything and support has to step in
failure_modes.likelihood_reason: Reset and lockout were built by different teams
failure_modes.detectability_reason: Needs a reset in the middle of a lockout run to show up
failure_modes.test_idea: Fail three times, reset the password, then fail twice and check the account is still open

failure_modes.title: The lockout message names the 30 minute duration but not when it started
failure_modes.effect: The shopper guesses when to try again, comes back early and calls support
failure_modes.cause: The lockout message prints a fixed duration with no start time and no countdown
failure_modes.severity_reason: Annoying, but the shopper does get in eventually
failure_modes.likelihood_reason: The message is already written this way
failure_modes.detectability_reason: Anyone reading the lockout message notices
failure_modes.test_idea: Lock an account and check the message says when the 30 minutes end

failure_modes.title: The failed attempt counter keeps counting after a successful sign-in on another device
failure_modes.effect: A shopper who signs in on their phone is still shut out on their laptop
failure_modes.cause: A successful sign-in resets the failed attempt counter for that session only
failure_modes.severity_reason: One device is blocked while another works
failure_modes.likelihood_reason: Session-scoped counters are a common shortcut
failure_modes.detectability_reason: Shows up only in a two-device run
failure_modes.test_idea: Fail three times on a laptop, sign in successfully on a phone, then fail twice on the laptop

failure_modes.title: The password reset endpoint has no rate limit of its own
failure_modes.effect: An attacker floods a shopper with reset mail and works around the sign-in lock
failure_modes.cause: The lock guards the sign-in form only, and reset requests are never counted
failure_modes.severity_reason: A way around the control this whole story is about
failure_modes.likelihood_reason: Someone has to go looking for the gap
failure_modes.detectability_reason: A quick script against the endpoint shows it
failure_modes.test_idea: Send 50 reset requests for one email in a minute and check they are throttled
